title: An explanation of why spacetime has one time and three space dimensions

concept.text: Strings 2000 problem 5 (proposed by Shamit Kachru, Sunil Mukhi and Hiroshi Ooguri): why does the universe appear to have one time and three space dimensions? Sources given: https://preskill.caltech.edu/millennium.html ; https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v54.i10.14_2.online.pdf ; https://x.com/martinmbauer/status/1779906631003697211.

page.title: Dynamical origin of spacetime dimensionality and signature
page.definition: A physical theory explains why observable spacetime has three extended spatial dimensions and one time dimension. It derives the Lorentzian signature—the distinction between timelike and spacelike directions—and the number of large spatial dimensions.

goal.need: Ten-dimensional superstring theory has 9 spatial directions and 1 time direction, whereas the observable universe has 3 spatial directions. Six spatial directions must therefore escape observation. Compactification, in which extra directions curl up too small to resolve, permits many choices. The Strings 2000 panel selected the explanation of the observed 1+3 split as one of its 10 unsolved problems.

completion.title: An independently verified derivation selects one time and three extended spatial dimensions.
completion.criterion: A physical theory derives why observable spacetime has exactly three extended spatial dimensions and one time dimension, rather than choosing these counts as background inputs. An independent calculation verifies the dimensional and signature selection, including the physical limits of any approximation or regulator used. This is a provisional Atlas test; no field-wide numerical confidence threshold or prescribed experiment was found.
completion.set_by: Atlas provisional criterion; no external acceptance test for the combined explanation was located.
completion.basis: Searches of the Strings 2000 statement, the NORDITA numerical-quantum-gravity roadmap, dimensional-selection papers and prize criteria found no shared acceptance test for this question. The question requires an explanation of both counts. Atlas provisionally requires a joint derivation and independent verification; recovering four dimensions or three expanding matrix directions alone does not settle it.

milestones.title: A quantum-gravity model recovers effective spacetime dimension 4 at large scales.
milestones.criterion: A model's measured effective spacetime dimension agrees with 4 at large scales; the convention sets no numerical tolerance. Spectral dimension measures the scaling of a diffusion return probability. The causal dynamical triangulations (CDT) preprint submitted on 12 May 2005 gave a fitted large-distance value 4.02 ± 0.10, using geometries of up to approximately 181,000 four-dimensional simplices and 400 diffusion measurements. CDT uses four-dimensional building blocks; this checks macroscopic recovery rather than explaining their dimension.
milestones.set_by: Numerical quantum-gravity community, as summarized by Glaser and Steinhaus in section 1.3.4 of their 2019 NORDITA workshop report.
milestones.threshold_quote: whether these generalized notions of dimension agree with our expectation of four space-time dimensions on large scales.

milestones.title: A matrix-model calculation selects 3 expanding spatial directions out of 9.
milestones.criterion: In the Lorentzian type IIB matrix model, exactly 3 eigenvalues of the spatial extent tensor grow after a critical time while the other 6 remain small, indicating rotational symmetry breaking from SO(9) to SO(3). Kim, Nishimura and Tsuchiya reported this at matrix size N = 16 and spatial block size n = 4. On 5 September 2019, Aoki and colleagues showed that the simulated expanding geometry had a singular Pauli-matrix structure caused by the approximation. This diagnostic alone does not establish smooth three-dimensional space.
milestones.set_by: Lorentzian type IIB matrix-model literature: Kim, Nishimura and Tsuchiya (2012), subsequently examined by Aoki and colleagues (2019). This diagnostic is specific to that framework.
milestones.threshold_quote: three out of nine spatial directions start to expand at some “critical time”, after which the space has SO(3) symmetry instead of SO(9).

milestones.title: One candidate theory derives 1 time direction and 3 extended spatial directions together.
milestones.criterion: One candidate theory derives both 3 extended spatial directions and 1 time direction without fixing either count as a background input, with its physical regulator limits specified. Greensite's massless one-loop mechanism requires more fermionic than bosonic degrees of freedom and a restricted signature ansatz. The 1994 follow-up also permits Lorentzian selection in 6 dimensions. The preprint submitted on 21 April 2026 reports smooth, real 3+1 expansion at matrix size N = 128 with auxiliary deformations; it does not establish this joint selection. That result is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: Atlas provisional criterion; no external milestone criterion for a joint derivation of both counts was located.

not_found: No field-wide acceptance test or prize rules for solving the combined dimensionality-and-signature question were found.
No published common milestone sequence leading to a joint explanation was found.
The draft's Physics Today PDF and X post could not be opened.

results.finding: CDT simulations with 400 diffusion measurements found a large-scale spectral dimension of 4.02 ± 0.1.
results.detail: The value is an asymptotic fit. Geometries contained up to approximately 181,000 four-simplices; CDT uses four-dimensional building blocks.

results.finding: CDT with 160,000 N₄,₁ simplices: large-distance spectral dimension 4.05 ± 0.17.
results.detail: The value is extrapolated from a fit and includes statistical and estimated systematic errors. CDT uses four-dimensional building blocks; the result tests macroscopic recovery.
results.quote:
We find that the long distance spectral dimension is consistent with the semiclassical dimensionality of 4, and that the spectral dimension smoothly decreases to a value consistent with

on short distance scales and for sufficiently fine lattice spacings.

results.finding: EDT simulations at 4,000, 8,000 and 16,000 four-simplices yielded a global Hausdorff dimension of 4.1 ± 0.3.
results.detail: The fitted dimension agrees with 4 within statistical uncertainty. The simulations use four-dimensional building blocks; the result tests macroscopic recovery of dimension.
results.quote:
A ﬁt designed to maximize the overlap between the curves with DH a free parameter leads to
a value DH = 4.1± 0.3, where the error is statistical only.

results.finding: Lorentzian type IIB matrix model, N = 16 and n = 4: 3 of 9 spatial extent eigenvalues grow after a critical time.
results.detail: The reported result suggests SO(9) breaking to SO(3). The simulation shown used κ = 4.0; the source does not establish a smooth three-dimensional space.
results.quote:
After the
critical time tc, three eigenvalues become larger, suggesting
that the SO(9) symmetry is spontaneously broken down to
SO(3).

results.finding: Lorentzian type IIB matrix simulation at N = 16, block size n = 6: 3 of 9 spatial directions expand.
results.detail: Aoki and colleagues found a singular Pauli-matrix structure and attributed it to the simulation’s approximation. The result does not establish smooth three-dimensional space.
results.quote:
The n × n spatial submatrices ¯Ai(t) (i = 1, ... ,9 )a t
each time t show that only three out of nine directions expand after some critical time, suggesting
the SSB of rotational SO(9) symmetry to SO(3).

results.finding: Greensite’s massless one-loop model selects Lorentzian signature in D = 4; no sample size applies.
results.detail: The signature ansatz allows only one potentially timelike direction, so the time-direction count is restricted from the outset. The result requires more fermionic than bosonic degrees of freedom and assumes a momentum cutoff; physical regulator limits are not established.
results.quote:
For nF > nB there is only one solution, namely, D = 4
dimensions and θ = ±π.

results.finding: One-loop field theory, sample size not applicable: Lorentzian signature can also be selected in D=6.
results.detail: The analysis uses a restricted single-Wick-angle signature ansatz and does not derive three extended spatial dimensions and one time direction without fixing either count. Its massive-field analysis also permits Lorentzian selection in six dimensions.
results.quote:
Mass eﬀects
lift this degeneracy, and we show that a dynamical origin of Lorentz ian signature is
also possible for (broken) supersymmetry theories in D=6 dimension s, in addition
to the more general non-supersymmetric case in D=4 dimensions.
